newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen end higher but shed some gains.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen end higher but shed some gains.

text.p: The key December three-month Euroyen futures contract ended higher but off the day's highs on Wednesday.
Falls in bank share prices in the morning re-ignited concern about Japan's financial system and led to buying of Euroyen futures, traders said.
Traders said Euroyen futures were sold in the afternoon as Tokyo share prices rose off the day's lows.

The December surged in the morning due to rumours that Nippon Credit Bank Ltd might hold an emergency media briefing. An NCB official later denied it had any such plan but later the bank announced it would hold a special briefing at 0800 GMT to deny recent market rumours.

Traders said the rumours had aroused speculation that the Bank of Japan will have to maintain its current low interest rate policy for some time and encouraged buying of Euroyen futures. Despite comments by an NCB official saying there is no cause for concern about the bank's financial health, worries about Japan's financial system will persist, traders said.
An NCB spokesman quoted the bank's senior managing director Tadao Iwaki as saying the bank's financial health was steadily recovering and its profitability was also improving.
The spokesman quoted Iwaki as saying there was no need to worry about the bank's financial health.
A trader for a long-term credit bank's securities unit said he expected the December to move in a range between 99.20 and 99.25 for the rest of the week.
The Bank of Japan injected a net 300 billion yen into the money market on Wednesday, maintaining its neutral stance.
Traders said the key overnight call rate was most heavily traded at 0.49 percent, which they said was likely to be the weighted average on Wednesday.
Tuesday's weighted average of the key overnight call rate was 0.50 percent.

About 170 billion yen worth of the key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.54 percent, the highest rate since August 30, 1996. Three-month CDs were issued at 0.53 percent on Tuesday.
One-month CDs were tagged with a sell quote of 0.51 percent and two-month CDs were offered at 0.54 percent.
